context.content: Emergency HVAC calls (no heat/no cool in extreme weather, gas leak, carbon monoxide) are classified Priority 1. Dispatch a technician within 2 hours. Notify the on-call supervisor immediately. Do not defer emergency calls.

Carbon monoxide or gas leak: advise customer to evacuate immediately and call 911. Do not dispatch HVAC technician until fire department clears the site. Create an incident report and notify the safety officer.

draft.body: I will treat this as an emergency HVAC request for Thursday. I will create a high‑urgency work order, prepare a Priority 1 dispatch for Thursday, and notify the on‑call supervisor immediately. Before I can assign and dispatch a technician I need the following details: site address/building, contact name and phone number for confirmation, a preferred time window on Thursday (AM/PM or specific hours), which specific HVAC unit/location (roof unit, AHU number, suite/floor), whether the failure is heating or cooling (or other), account/PO number or contract/SLA if applicable, authorization for emergency/after‑hours charges, and any access instructions or gate codes. If you suspect a gas leak or carbon monoxide, evacuate the building and call 911; we will not dispatch until emergency responders clear the site.

issues_found: "I will treat this as an emergency HVAC request for Thursday." — This phrasing implies deferring the emergency to Thursday; the retrieved ops-manual mandates Priority 1 emergency HVAC calls be dispatched within 2 hours and not deferred, so treating it as an emergency 'for Thursday' is potentially incorrect or non-compliant.

"prepare a Priority 1 dispatch for Thursday" — Scheduling a Priority 1 dispatch specifically for Thursday contradicts the requirement to dispatch a technician within 2 hours for Priority 1 emergencies. The draft gives the impression of scheduling rather than immediate dispatch.

"Before I can assign and dispatch a technician I need the following details: site address/building, contact name and phone number..." — The ops-manual requires dispatch within 2 hours for Priority 1; saying you cannot assign/dispatch until these details are provided misrepresents the procedural requirement to initiate dispatch promptly and gather missing information in parallel when necessary.

"If you suspect a gas leak or carbon monoxide, evacuate the building and call 911; we will not dispatch until emergency responders clear the site." — While evacuation and awaiting emergency responders is correct, the draft omits the ops-manual instruction to create an incident report and notify the safety officer for carbon monoxide or gas leak incidents, leaving out an actionable requirement.

Action item: 'Confirm appointment with customer for Thursday (time window and contact phone required)' — Framing the response as confirming an appointment for Thursday conflicts with the 'do not defer emergency calls' and 'dispatch within 2 hours' requirements. This could mislead staff to treat a Priority 1 as a scheduled appointment rather than an immediate dispatch.

Caveats list missing address/contact/time etc. — While accurate about missing caller-provided details, the draft does not state that dispatch should proceed immediately despite missing details (per ops-manual), which may leave the operator thinking dispatch must wait for all information.
